A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spark3D study. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, method ablations, low-data evaluations, and generalization tests in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds ABCD-pretrained checkpoint evaluations and BTCV CT segmentation experiments.

M1.justification: The residual encoder U-Net, sparse convolutions and normalization, mask tokens, densification convolutions, masked L2 objective, masking strategy, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. S3D-B becomes S3D, while S3D-L is presented as S3D-Long; the reported training-budget revision belongs to E3.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds pre-training on approximately 41k ABCD T1/T2 MRI scans and evaluation on BTCV CT multi-organ segmentation, substantially extending the original coverage. The original MRI datasets remain. The headline change from 44k to 39k reflects filtering to 39,168 scans already documented in v1.

E2.justification: The new BTCV comparison includes directly evaluated HySparK and unpretrained MedNeXt+ViT, plus literature-reported vox2vec, SUP, MAE, SimMIM, and SparK results. Original MRI test baselines remain, but the development-set comparator results in v1 Table 1(c) are no longer presented as such: v2 Table 2(c) instead duplicates the ABCD comparison.

E3.justification: BTCV introduces a shared five-fold evaluation, explicitly distinguished from literature results using an unspecified 80/20 split. Appendix B changes the stated long-model budget from 1M to 1.25M steps while retaining batch size 48, learning rate 0.03, and identical scores; this does not establish rerunning. Existing MRI preprocessing and split procedures remain stable.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds a comparison of private-data and ABCD pre-training, examining performance retention with an alternative training source. Existing masking, sparsification, low-data, training-duration, input-stem, and MRI generalization analyses remain. The development-set compound-scaling comparison disappears, while its test-set scores are retained in Table 12.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrapped ranking stability and identical five-fold input-stem results with means and standard deviations (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 8). No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced. BTCV cross-validation changes evaluation design.

E6.justification: New results include ABCD versus private pre-training at 74.34 versus 74.88 mean DSC over D1-D10, and BTCV scores of 84.99 for S3D, 84.63 for fixed scratch, and 80.67 for HySparK under shared folds. Retained MRI scores and original appendix ablation values are identical. Development comparison entries disappear, Table 12 reports four-method rankings, and the dataset figure changes some proportions, including FLAIR from 19.5% to 8.7%.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs. The mathematical descriptions of reconstruction, masking, and sampling remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claim of approximately three DSC points over dynamic nnU-Net remains. The introduction shifts from proposing a 'novel' sparse MAE paradigm toward explicitly acknowledging existing MAE concepts and emphasizing configuration, evaluation, and ablation contributions. The abstract removes the specific mean-rank-of-two-among-seven claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit head-and-neck MRI scope limitations and baseline-exclusion rationale. Appendix C attributes the ABCD performance gap to training-data diversity, while Appendix B cautions against transferring longer-training expectations from general vision. Existing interpretations concerning resolution, unseen MRI modalities, and data curation remain.

D1.justification: v2 announces ABCD-pretrained public weights and explains why the original clinical-data weights cannot be shared. It documents the approximately 41k-scan, balanced T1/T2 corpus and use of a public HySparK checkpoint for BTCV. Most implementation settings, hardware information, training times, and the code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated related-work section covering general MAEs, medical MAEs, and other medical SSL methods, alongside a table assessing ten methods against the stated pitfalls. New citations include AMAES, MAPSeg, GVSL, VideoMAE, and vox2vec. Positioning more explicitly emphasizes validation of existing MAE ideas.

P1.justification: The contribution narrative is substantially rewritten, related work is inserted before the method section, scaling moves into a separate appendix, and additional results gain dedicated subsections. The conclusion gains an explicit limitations paragraph. Terminology and prose are edited throughout, including model renaming and removal of the unfinished 'XXX' placeholder.

P2.justification: The paper switches to two-column layout and extensively reformats tables. The pipeline figure is removed; a performance-summary plot and related-work matrix are added. The dataset figure is redrawn and moved to the appendix, ranking plots change to six methods, and long-model scores are redisplayed separately. Table 2(c) duplicates Table 5 under an inconsistent development-results caption.

improvement.justification: The ABCD checkpoint alternative, BTCV evaluation, and expanded research positioning add useful evidence and practical value. However, v2 replaces the development comparison with a miscaptioned ABCD duplicate, retains unexplained seven-method ranks in a six-method table, and states 1.25M training steps while retaining the earlier 32-fold scaling claim. These reporting regressions coexist with the benefits, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
